scope: Six additional missing IWW prisoners with actual custodial service established; preserve existing profiles and uncertain endpoints.

march-p7.label: One Big Union Monthly, March 1920, printed p.7: Ralph Bergdorff individual custody entry; scan image reviewed.

april-p13.label: John Engdahl / Northwest District Defense Committee, One Big Union Monthly, April 1920, printed p.13: named Ritzville and Prosser defendants explicitly serving sentences; full page image reviewed.

jacobson-study.label: John E. Haynes, Revolt of the Timber Beasts, Minnesota History 42 (Spring 1971), pp.163,173: Local490 leadership, January4 arrest, sentence and actual imprisonment while a successor took over; original historical-society PDF text reviewed.

jacobson-distinction.label: Victoria Daily Times, August30,1918, p.16, IWWs Sentenced at Chicago Today: Charles Jacobson of Duluth and Charles Jacobs of Denver are separately listed in the same sentencing report. Both columns checked in original page image.

prisoner.name: Charles Jacobson
prisoner.description: Charles Jacobson was secretary-treasurer of the IWW mine workers union at Virginia, Minnesota. He was jailed in January 1917 during suppression of the northern Minnesota lumber strike, and another organizer took over his duties.

cases.charges: Municipal charge of lurking and lying in wait with intent to do mischief
cases.sentence: Arrested January 4, 1917 at the union office in Virginia, Minnesota. Received a $100 fine or ninety days in jail; the historical study confirms he served jail time while Richard Mattson took over. Exact release and completed time served are unverified; ninety days is not entered as documented actual duration.

case_research.custody_evidence: Historical study explicitly describes actual sentence service and replacement in union duties, establishing sustained custody rather than merely a fine alternative.

The later federal sentence is an additional research lead; its actual custody dates are not inferred here. No birth year derived from age28.

prisoner.name: J. Callahan
prisoner.description: J. Callahan appears in the IWW Northwest District prisoner register as a Prosser defendant convicted of criminal syndicalism. The April 1920 report explicitly states that the named defendants were serving their jail sentences.

cases.sentence: The arrest register dates the Prosser entry November 16, 1919 and records a conviction with a sentence of six months to one year, explicitly being served. Prison admission day, sentencing day, completed time served and eventual release are unknown. Do not use the full nominal sentence as actual duration or assume uninterrupted detention from the arrest date.

prisoner.name: Ralph Bergdorff
prisoner.description: Ralph Bergdorff appears in the IWW prisoner register as a detainee held for six months at Spokane in 1918. The entry also describes earlier Bellingham confinement and a later return there.

cases.charges: Detention during the IWW crackdown; precise charge unspecified
cases.sentence: Rearrested at Spokane in 1918 and held in county jail for six months. The entry also describes an earlier one-year Bellingham sentence, a jail escape and reincarceration at Bellingham in January 1919. Only the explicitly documented six-month Spokane interval is counted here; exact dates, possible breaks in custody and eventual release are unknown.

case_research.custody_evidence: The individual entry expressly reports six months actually held in Spokane County Jail.
